subject: SprintLane renewal — uplift request, co-term and packaging options
messages:
From: Avery Brooks <avery@sprintlane.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-27T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + mid-contract top-up

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our side: usage spiked this quarter (NLP feature rollout) and we need an uplift of ~40% of our committed capacity for the next 6 months. Procurement wants this to co-term with our existing contract (renewal scheduled 2026-11-30).

Two asks from SprintLane:
- Can you provide a pricing path for a temporary top-up (6 months) that does not reprice the existing baseline commitment?
- Any flexibility on discount bands if we agree to annualize the extra capacity at renewal (Dec 1)?

Also copying Procurement (Priya) and Legal (Tom) since there will likely be an amendment + vendor review.

Appreciate a quick ballpark so we can present to our CFO by Friday.

Best,
Avery
Avery Brooks
Head of Platform, SprintLane
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Brooks <avery@sprintlane.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@procurement.sprintlane.com>, Tom Everett <tom.everett@legal.sprintlane.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + mid-contract top-up

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear ask. Quick thoughts and next steps below.

Short answer: yes, we can support a timeboxed uplift + co-term pathway. We typically do two options depending on how you want to handle billing/credits:

Option A — Temporary top-up (6 months):
- Add a temporary bucket at a modest uplift discount (list + 10% off baseline committed rate)
- Usage beyond the top-up billed monthly, no change to baseline pricing
- No contract change required, but we can issue an amendment for audit

Option B — Annualize at renewal (preferred if you want lower unit cost):
- Convert the temporary top-up into committed capacity at renewal (Dec 1)
- We can apply a one-time credit for the duration of the temporary top-up towards the annualized commitment (reduces net-first-year cost)
- Deeper discount bands available when annualized (additional 7–12% depending on total committed volume)

I'll loop in Marcus (sales lead) and Jordan (pricing/finance) to build a concrete workbook. Attaching a working pricing sheet and an SLA amendment draft for your legal team to scan.

Can we schedule a 30-min alignment tomorrow to walk the workbook and quick ROI math?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0183

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx (pricing model), SLA_amendment_v2.pdf (amendment stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SprintLane uplift — discount guardrails and packaging

Soojin/Jordan — quick internal note before we present. Key constraints from finance/legal and recommended play: 

1) Discount guardrails:
- For temporary top-ups (<= 6 months) keep discounts conservative: max 10% off baseline list. Anything deeper requires annualization commitment.
- For annualize-at-renewal pathway we can tier discounts: 5% @ +25% total commit, 10% @ +50%, 15% @ +100% (these are conditional on a 12-month committed conversion).

2) Credits and billing:
- Offer a usage credit equal to 50% of the uplift fees paid during the 6-month top-up, applied if SprintLane converts that uplift to a committed annual increase at renewal. This preserves cash flow for us while giving them downside protection.

3) Packaging:
- Recommend framing as "Top-up Bridge + Conversion Credit" in the amendment. Keeps the amendment short and prevents baseline reprice risk.

4) Legal touchpoints:
- SLA amendment is small but Tom will want indemnity + data residency clause checked.

Soojin — propose we present a workbook with two concrete numbers (Option A and Option B) and a one-slide summary for Priya/CFO. Jordan, can you run 3 scenarios in the pricing sheet: conservative (10% uplift @ 0% conversion), mid (40% uplift @ 50% conversion), aggressive (40% uplift @ 100% conversion) and return by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Sales — East, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Brooks <avery@sprintlane.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@procurement.sprintlane.com>, Tom Everett <tom.everett@legal.sprintlane.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + mid-contract top-up

Avery — thanks for the patience while we ran scenarios. Attached is the workbook (redwood-pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx) with the three scenarios Marcus requested and a one-page summary below.

One-page summary (high-level):
- Temporary top-up (6 months) — 40% uplift: additional $28k/mo at list; offered top-up discount = 10% -> $25.2k/mo. Billed monthly. No change to baseline.
- Conversion credit if annualized at renewal: 50% of uplift fees paid during the 6-month window (credit applied to first-year annualized uplift commitment).
- If SprintLane converts the uplift to an increased annual commitment on 2026-12-01, net-first-year uplift discount ranges from 7–12% depending on final committed volume (see scenarios tab).

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm which option you want to pursue (A: temporary top-up only or B: top-up with conversion path to annualize).
2) If B, confirm the expected annualized uplift percent so we can draft a short amendment with the conversion credit language.
3) Tom/Priya — if you can flag any must-have legal clauses this week, we’ll get a clean amendment to you for signature.

If helpful, I can book a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk the workbook and ROI math.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0183

Attachments included: redwood-pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx, SLA_amendment_v2.pdf
